items.title: Orrin Evans interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 22, 2018
items.q: Well we are a band for tonight... because I’m from Philly and Reggie’s West Virginia... figuring out how — we speak the same language

ctx.x: Audience members are sometimes intrigued by that. How do you put on what can look like a rehearsed or like you’re a band, and you’re not really a band. How does that work?

Well we are a band for tonight. And you know I do hear that a lot, “Oh you’ve just joined them and you guys just met?” Those kinds of things. But I guess that’s what we’ve been doing all our lives practicing and practicing performing music, so then if you’re all speaking that same language, you know, and that language is the language of music, it’s really easy to sit down and play with some people that speak the same language. Now sometimes things happen where we might speak a different dialect. You know we’re…
There’s a certain etiquette to a jazz performance. Can you learn that in jazz school?
